items.title: Validate durable-resume input in core before side effects
items.rationale: roadmap 0.2.0 item 1 / review blocker 1: prepareAgentRunResume treats any decision other than 'approve'/'deny' as 'no decision given' and proceeds to claim the checkpoint and execute the suspended tool; resolveRunDecisions assumes typed entries so malformed untyped batches crash with raw TypeErrors. One assertValidAgentRunResume in agent-approval.ts invoked at the top of prepareAgentRunResume covers all four public entrypoints (lifecycle resume/resumeStream and free resumeAgentRun/resumeAgentRunStream). Reuses AgentDecisionError codes, HARD_MAX_PENDING_DECISIONS, MAX_DECISION_REASON_BYTES, MAX_ELICITATION_BYTES from the preserved contracts-run-state surface. Server readAgentResume/readAgentDecisions stay unchanged (defense in depth).

items.title: Isolate work-tool subprocess environments and linearize output capture
securityTests: T5 token env override of reserved keys
items.rationale: roadmap 0.2.0 item 2 / review blocker 2: createCliRunner builds the child env as {...process.env, ...options.env, HOME, CLIMICROSOFT365_DISABLETELEMETRY}, so every ambient variable reaches the child (manual proof: PRISM_PROOF_SECRET leaked); binary/configDir accept relative paths; defaultExec accumulates output with repeated Buffer.concat (worst-case O(n^2)). Fix: package-local buildCliEnvironment (minimal fixed allow-list base, then explicit options.env, then reserved fixed controls set last; NUL/casing/count/byte validation) + collectOutput (chunk array, one final concat, cap kill) + path.isAbsolute checks. No new public exports (Task 0 approved module-private helpers in cli.ts only); docker/native exact-env behavior is the preserved precedent.

items.title: Ship explicit sandbox capabilities and conservative compatibility metadata
items.rationale: roadmap 0.2.0 item 3 / review blocker 3: SandboxCodingComposition.containmentClaim is computed from workspace wiring alone (backendsBound && !mixedWiringAllowed && warnings.length === 0) so native (no filesystem isolation) and duck-typed custom adapters can claim containment. Fix: additive SandboxCapabilities {workspaceCoherent, filesystemIsolated, networkIsolated, egressRestricted, processIsolated, privilegeIsolated} on SandboxAdapter with omission => all false, resolveSandboxCapabilities in sandbox-coding-operations.ts, truthful built-in metadata (native filesystemIsolated false; docker networkIsolated only for mode none, egressRestricted only with attestation, privilegeIsolated false), containmentClaim retained as @deprecated conservative conjunction. CONSTRAINT: src/__tests__/docs.test.ts:1262 asserts docs/coding-security.md still includes 'containmentClaim', so docs keep the deprecated term. Egress validation primitives (egress/) are preserved surface.

items.title: Add public-JavaScript, packed-consumer, and named threat-suite regressions
items.rationale: roadmap 0.2.0 mandatory regression matrix items 1-3 / review blocker evidence: the original resume defect passed TypeScript declarations and existed only at runtime, so regressions must run against built public entrypoints and a fresh packed plain-JavaScript consumer (install-smoke harness), not private source imports. scripts/phase20-security.test.mjs wires into security:threat-suites; sandbox-browser.yml records Docker/native capability evidence and is a required protected gate (missing => 0.2.0 blocked, never a passing skip). release.yml retains the phase-20 security report in publish prerequisites only if sdk:ready does not already cover it (conditional edit; existence is the only done-marker).
